title: Sanitization proxy for trace snapshots and immutable access ledger
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Incoming trace snapshots and telemetry events sometimes contain PII or sensitive tokens which currently traverse the metrics/log pipeline before any tenant-scoped redaction. That increases blast radius for downstream processors and complicates retention enforcement. Goal: introduce a lightweight sanitization proxy that runs at the pipeline ingress to handle deterministic field-level redaction, configurable tenant policies, and produce an immutable access ledger entry for every access/redaction decision. The proxy should be pluggable (room for heuristic classifiers later), preserve trace context for debugging, and emit compact audit records to the audit-store with a tenant identifier and reason codes.
acceptance_criteria: Sanitization proxy sits in front of the trace/log ingestion path and processes >=99% of incoming events for the test traffic profile without adding >12ms median latency
Field-level redaction rules are configurable per-tenant via Console policies and can be updated without restart
Proxy emits an immutable access ledger event for every processed trace/log that includes: event_id, tenant_id, redaction_applied (yes/no), rule_id, actor (system/ingress), timestamp
Audit-store ingestion demonstrates queryable access records and can return all accesses for a tenant in <500ms for 30-day window in staging
End-to-end test showing original sensitive field removed for tenants with 'strict' policy and preserved (masked) for 'permissive' tenants
Integration tests validate trace continuity (trace_id preserved) across proxy and downstream collectors
Security review completed and threat-model notes attached to ticket
Rollout plan includes canary in a single region and feature-flag gating with automatic rollback
